correctness.rationale: The frozen opening describes the full-state maps as nonconjugate under an all-n quantifier; at n=1 both maps are constant zero. The repaired RESULT.md explicitly separates this case and proves nonconjugacy for every n≥2 by different indegrees of the unique fixed points. In that proof Rule 18 has at least the two constant preimages and the n distinct one-zero words, whereas Rule 126's zero preimages are exactly the two constant words. The recurrent and basin claims survive unchanged. Boolean evaluation of HD gives one iff the triple is nonconstant; DH gives (1−b)(a XOR c), so repeated-neighbor conventions do not affect the factorization. Iterating yields T^t=HS^(t−1)D, and HS^(t−1) is a two-sided inverse to D between t-fold fixed sets. Intertwining with time and rotations therefore preserves periods, joint fixed counts and all combined stabilizers. Every even-parity cyclic difference has exactly two lifts, obtained by choosing the first bit; odd differences have none. The factor map carries the eventual orbit of every point to the uniquely matched orbit, giving the parity-sliced basin law. A fresh truth-table enumeration at n=1,2,4 confirmed the boundary contrast and reproduced the n=4 image sizes 7 and 6 and matching basin vectors (12,2,2) versus (8,4,4). The frozen code, notes, and outputs were inspected; all finite-ring claims use the proof, not extrapolation from recorded program output.
